h2_complement.note: sign from the title ('promote macular degeneration'). The mechanism credits 'genetic variants in ARMS2 and C3', but the chain starts at the proteins, so the subjects are the proteins

h3_apoptosis.note: title 'exacerbates', mechanism 'drives the clinical progression' -> progression; the chain's last step (h3_apoptosis.2, 'contributes to macular tissue loss and AMD') reads as risk. h3_apoptosis.1 targets apoptosis of retinal endothelial cells (a refinement) and h3_apoptosis.2 starts at apoptosis in general, so the chain does not connect

findings.detail: every hypothesis reaches AMD only through an associated_with step with polarity 'unknown', so none of the five gene claims has a route, whatever the earlier steps say

the notes state a direction ('Overactivation of the complement system causes chronic retinal inflammation'; 'Increased cell death ... contributes to macular tissue loss and AMD') that the structured polarity field leaves 'unknown'; the prose direction is lost in the structured output
process-to-AMD steps cite GWAS Catalog rows for single variants near CETP, LIPC, C3 and TNFRSF10A; each row states a variant-AMD association and names no process

the run's strongest evidence (seven genome-wide GWAS rows: rs17231506-T decrease, rs2414577-C decrease, rs36212733-C increase, rs10490924-T OR 2.76, rs11569415-A decrease, rs2230199 OR 1.43 allele unreported, rs13278062-T decrease) has no variant step to attach to, so none of it reaches a claim

rs2414577 is cited as a LIPC variant, but the record's Ensembl context places it inside ALDH1A2 (distance 0), while its functional class is intergenic and LIPC lies 22 kb (Ensembl) or 44 kb (NCBI) away; rs17231506 is intergenic, 1.3 kb from CETP
rs36212733 and rs10490924 sit in ARMS2 and HTRA1-AS1, and the rs10490924 study reports ARMS2 and HTRA1 as genes; the run treats the locus as ARMS2 alone
LIPC's UniProt text (and the run's own note) says it hydrolyses triglycerides and phospholipids in lipoproteins; it never mentions cholesterol, yet the step is LIPC leads_to cholesterol metabolism

the only ARMS2-C3 link cited is one STRING edge (combined 0.70, mostly text-mining 0.62, experiments 0.24); it states an unsigned link and nothing more, and nothing cited puts ARMS2 in the complement pathway, as the mechanism and the step note ('functionally interacts') claim
the ChEMBL record says only that pegcetacoplan targets C3 and is approved; it names no indication, so it does not link complement activation to AMD
the step's context says AMD (MONDO:0005150), but the cited single-cell record compares donors with AMD 7 (MONDO:0012419, the HTRA1-caused form; 430 cells) against normal

the single-cell record cited for 'expressed in retinal endothelial cells' shows TNFRSF10A in 2.5% of 161 disease cells against 4.4% of normal ones (lower in disease, low overall), and its disease is macular degeneration (MONDO:0003004), not AMD; the run does not mention this
h1_cholesterol.2 starts at LIPC, not at the object of h1_cholesterol.1: the 'chain' is two parallel gene steps into one node, which is fine for composition but not a sequence

h3_apoptosis.1 ends at apoptosis of retinal blood vessel endothelial cells (its context, the title and the falsification), but h3_apoptosis.2 starts at apoptosis in general ('the retinal vasculature or RPE'), so the chain breaks; no cited text puts TNFRSF10A or apoptosis in either cell
